newsitem.title: USA: USDA wants to allow imports of some pork products.
newsitem.headline: USDA wants to allow imports of some pork products.

text.p: The Agriculture Department said Friday it wants to allow imports of sliced and pre-packaged dry-cured pork products under certain conditions.
A proposed rule will be published in Monday's Federal Register, and public comments on the proposal should be submitted by June 13, the Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) said.

The proposed rule would allow pork products that come from whole, dry-cured hams, pork shoulders and pork loins that meet APHIS requirements. The slicing and packaging must be done at an APHIS-approved facility located in the same region of the same country as the place where the pork was dry-cured, the agency said.
The conditions would allow APHIS to verify the meat's origin, how it was processed and whether it was handled in a manner that ensures it is free of disease.
